📌 Data Leak Scams: Why Your Wallet Company Will Never Call You

Main Points
⏺ When a shop or service leaks customer data, scammers get your name, phone and address
⏺ They then call or write pretending to be "support" from your wallet brand
⏺ This post explains how these scams work and how to shut them down in one sentence



1️⃣ Core Idea — A leaked order list tells scammers exactly who owns a crypto wallet. That makes their fake "security alert" sound real. A reseller connected to Trezor recently reported a breach of roughly 27,000 orders.
2️⃣ Why It Happens — The leak doesn't touch your coins. It gives criminals your contact details, so the attack moves from your device to your trust.
3️⃣ Example — You get a call: "Your wallet was compromised, read us your recovery phrase so we can secure it." The caller knows your name and what you bought.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — Phone calls, SMS, emails with "urgent firmware updates", and even paper letters with a QR code to a fake site.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — No real wallet company will ever call you or ask for your seed phrase. Hang up, ignore the link, and only use the official app or website you type in yourself.
Final Thoughts

A data leak is a warning, not a theft. Your funds are safe as long as the seed phrase never leaves your hands — and nobody who asks for it is on your side.

The Speaker May Have to Wait for Silence

The Knesset began debating Tuesday afternoon whether to replace Speaker Amir Ohana of Likud with Matan Kahana, Gadi Eisenkot’s candidate from Yashar. Kahana has the votes. The Joint List and Ra’am confirmed they will back him, giving Eisenkot’s bloc the simple majority it needs.

Likud is mobilizing ministers and lawmakers to drag out the debate. Ministers generally have unlimited speaking time, but the Knesset’s legal advisers say a minister’s remarks must be reasonably limited when parliament elects its own speaker. 

If the debate runs on, Eisenkot’s bloc could invoke Article 98 of the Knesset rules to cut it short. Likud calls that heavy-handed.

Likud has fielded its own candidate, Ofir Katz, after Kahana turned down its support on condition that he not appoint Arab lawmakers as deputy speakers. 

Shas will vote for Katz, and Degel HaTorah’s four lawmakers have been instructed to do the same.

🌐 Cryptocurrency exchange MEXC has announced that it will discontinue its Global Card payment services on Nov. 18 at 15:30 UTC, less than two weeks after U.S. authorities issued an order restricting its access to the American financial system. The exchange did not identify the issuing partner or specify whether its decision was directly related to the recent enforcement action by the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).

📊 During the maintenance period, customers could transfer their remaining card balances to their exchange accounts, while transactions initiated before the suspension remained subject to normal settlement procedures. MEXC had initially described the interruption as temporary but has now confirmed that the service will not resume as scheduled.

🔗 Cardholders could receive cashback ranging from 4% to 10%, with monthly rewards capped at up to 800 USDT depending on their eligibility. Applications were already unavailable to U.S. residents under the exchange’s regional restrictions. Customers using the card for recurring payments have been advised to cancel their subscriptions or register alternative payment methods to avoid interruptions once the card becomes inactive.

Cats meowed more when a person was present, suggesting they direct the sound at humans who can help. In a Brazilian study led by Naila Fukimoto of the University of São Paulo, 38 cats faced an unreachable treat. They meowed 86 times with a person in the room, versus 20 times alone, and often looked between the person and the container.

Published in Animal Behaviour, the findings support the idea that meows are aimed at people. The authors caution that the study involved a small group of food-focused, vocal cats and just one scenario, so not every meow is a demand.
